s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and syncope following alcohol ingestion with a prolonged time course
salient_findings: Recurrent abdominal pain after alcohol ingestion
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions on ECG
key_facts: Patient presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope
Symptoms occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion
Symptoms lasted 5-10 minutes
Syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Patient has a history of hypertension
Patient has a history of smoking and alcohol overconsumption
High-sensitivity troponin I was normal
Serum potassium was normal
ECG showed high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ECG showed ST segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF
Coronary angiography showed 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA

shortlist.label: Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of long-term alcohol overconsumption and presented with symptoms consistent with cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Vasovagal Syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced syncope after large alcohol intake, which could trigger vasovagal syncope

shortlist.label: Alcoholic Autonomic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of long-term alcohol overconsumption and presented with symptoms consistent with autonomic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Variant Angina
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST segment elevations, which could be indicative of variant angina

shortlist.label: Tako-Tsubo Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with symptoms consistent with cardiomyopathy and had a history of alcohol overconsumption, which could trigger Tako-Tsubo cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's long history of alcohol overconsumption, recurrent symptoms after alcohol ingestion, and ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Vasovagal Syncope
rejected.why: While syncope is a symptom, the presence of significant ECG abnormalities and the temporal relationship with alcohol ingestion suggest a more complex cardiac issue.

rejected.label: Alcoholic Autonomic Neuropathy
rejected.why: This condition could explain some symptoms but does not fully account for the cardiac-specific findings like high-degree atrioventricular block and ST segment elevations.

rejected.label: Variant Angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG findings do not typically align with variant angina, which is more closely associated with coronary artery spasm.

rejected.label: Tako-Tsubo Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar ECG changes, the patient's long-standing symptoms and history of alcohol abuse point more towards a chronic condition like alcoholic cardiomyopathy rather than an acute stress-induced cardiomyopathy.
